findings.title: [P2] Normalize absolute paths before excluding dot-prefixed words
findings.body: An evaluated agent can bypass outside-path detection with `cat /./root/private.txt`. ABS_WORD captures the path, but this branch discards it before outside() can normalize it to `/root/private.txt`. This lets reads outside the permitted roots escape contamination reporting. Normalize candidates before applying root checks, and restrict any relative-tail exception to verified shell-token context.
findings.description: An evaluated agent can bypass outside-path detection with `cat /./root/private.txt`. ABS_WORD captures the path, but this branch discards it before outside() can normalize it to `/root/private.txt`. This lets reads outside the permitted roots escape contamination reporting. Normalize candidates before applying root checks, and restrict any relative-tail exception to verified shell-token context.
findings.failure_mode: An evaluated agent can bypass outside-path detection with `cat /./root/private.txt`.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve executable expansions when stripping heredocs
findings.body: Unquoted Bash heredocs execute command substitutions, so their bodies are not necessarily inert data. For example, `cat <<EOF\n$(cat /root/private.txt)\nEOF` reads the outside file and prints its contents, but strip_heredocs() reduces the scanned command to `cat <<HEREDOC`. The original command was scanned before this change. Preserve and inspect executable expansions in unquoted heredocs instead of removing their entire bodies.

findings.failure_mode: Unquoted Bash heredocs execute command substitutions, so their bodies are not necessarily inert data.

findings.description: grader 1.2.2 strips every heredoc body from the Bash command before the absolute-path scan on the premise that heredoc text is 'data being written'. That premise is false whenever the heredoc feeds an interpreter: `bash <<EOF`, `sh -s <<EOF`, `python3 - <<EOF`, `node - <<EOF`, `sudo -s <<EOF`. Any `cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `open('/mnt/hidden/tests.py')` or `ls /srv/...` inside such a body is executed by the sandbox but never reaches the ABS_WORD loop, so `outside_path` can no longer fire. The hidden/suite/repo substring scans still see the full value, but the path leak check is the only one that catches arbitrary out-of-sandbox reads.
findings.failure_mode: An evaluated agent (or a model that habitually writes `python3 - <<'EOF'` scripts) reads files outside the allowed roots and the run is graded as uncontaminated; eval scores are inflated by access to data the contamination control is meant to detect.
findings.suggested_fix: Only strip heredoc bodies when the receiving command is a known pure sink (cat/tee/dd with a file target, `> file` redirection). When the heredoc is piped into an interpreter or shell (bash, sh, zsh, python*, node, perl, ruby, awk, sudo, env, xargs), scan the body with the same ABS_WORD loop. Alternatively keep scanning the body and instead whitelist only the specific prose patterns that caused the false positives.

findings.description: Several new skip rules are keyed on lexical shape rather than on the normalised path, and each one is trivially satisfiable for a real, resolvable path: (1) `w.startswith("/.")` skips `/./root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/./home/x/.aws/credentials`, `/./mnt/hidden/...` which the kernel resolves identically to the undotted path (`R=/./root; cat $R/.ssh/id_rsa` also passes since `=/./root` begins with `/.`); (2) after_closing_quote treats a word glued to a preceding quote as a path tail, so `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` or `cat ''/mnt/secret` (empty string followed by the path, a legal shell no-op) is skipped although it is the absolute path itself; (3) `"=" in w` and the `/,` prefix drop any word containing `=` or starting `/,` without checking whether it still normalises to a sensitive location. The existing `//` skip is already a bypass (`//root/...` resolves on Linux); the new rules add three more that require no special filesystem state.
findings.failure_mode: An agent reads hidden tests, credentials, or host files outside the sandbox roots using a path spelled `/./...`, `""/...` or `''/...`; the grader records contaminated=null/false and the trial is scored as clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply os.path.normpath (and strip surrounding/adjacent empty quotes) to the candidate first, then decide: skip only if the normalised path is still single-component, still begins with a dot-component, or is inside the allowed roots. For after_closing_quote, require that the text between the opening and closing quote is non-empty (an empty `""`/`''` does not make the following word a tail). Treat `//`-prefixed words the same way.

findings.description: For Bash the former case-insensitive substring check (`"hidden" in val.lower()`) is replaced by HIDDEN_TOKEN, which is case-sensitive (only `HIDDEN` or lowercase `hidden`) and only fires when `hidden` is adjacent to `/ . _ = -`. Natural probe commands now pass: `find . -iname '*hidden*'` (quote before, `*` after), `ls -d *hidden*`, `grep -ril hidden .`, `cat 'hidden tests/test_x.py'`, `ls "hidden tests"`, and any mixed case such as `cat Hidden/tests.py` or `ls HiddenTests` (Linux filesystems are case-sensitive but the detection no longer is). The non-Bash tools keep the old behaviour, so the weakening is Bash-only yet Bash is the richest channel.
findings.failure_mode: The agent enumerates or reads the hidden test directory through Bash using a globbed, quoted or mixed-case spelling and is not flagged `hidden`; recall/hidden_tests scores become contaminated without detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the token regex case-insensitive and treat quotes, globs and whitespace as token delimiters: e.g. `(?i)(?<![a-z])hidden(?![a-z])` applied to the command with heredoc prose excluded, or keep the old substring check and whitelist only prose inside heredoc/echo bodies (the actual false-positive source). At minimum add `'"*?\s` to both the lookbehind and lookahead sets and use re.I.

findings.description: in_quotes decides a one-component sensitive word (`/root`, `/home`, `/mnt`, `/media`, `/srv`) is quoted pattern text when the count of `'` or `"` before it is odd, counting raw characters with no awareness of nesting or escaping. Any earlier apostrophe inside a double-quoted string poisons the parity for the rest of the command: `echo "don't"; cd /root && cat .ssh/id_rsa`, `git commit -m "it's done" ; ls /home`, or `# can't` followed by `cd /mnt`. The comment already accepts `cd '/root/'` as a gap; the parity bug widens it to any command where the agent emits an odd quote earlier, which is common in commit messages and echo text.
findings.failure_mode: `cd /root`, `cd /home`, `cd /mnt` followed by relative reads escapes contamination detection whenever the command text happens to (or is crafted to) contain an unmatched apostrophe before the path word.
findings.suggested_fix: Use shlex-style tokenisation (shlex.split with posix=True, falling back to the raw scan on ValueError) to determine whether the word is a standalone argument versus inside a quoted literal, or drop the in_quotes exemption for SENSITIVE_SINGLE words entirely and accept the grep-pattern false positive, which is the safer failure direction for an integrity control.

findings.description: HEREDOC is compiled with re.S and contains `(?:.*?\n)*?` where `.` also matches newline. Each newline in the candidate body can be consumed by either `.*?` or the explicit `\n`, so when the terminator never matches (an unterminated `<<EOF`, a terminator with trailing text, or a `<<WORD` appearing inside a quoted string) the engine backtracks exponentially in the number of newlines. The input is the agent's own Bash command text from transcripts/events-*.jsonl, so an evaluated agent can hang the grader by emitting one command containing `<<EOF` followed by a few dozen newlines with no terminator.
findings.failure_mode: ablation-grade.sh hangs or hits LOA_EVAL_GRADE_TIMEOUT_S on an agent-controlled transcript; the trial is rowed infrastructure_error/ungraded instead of being scored, letting an agent escape grading of a bad run.

findings.description: `git log --all` / `git reflog` probes are downgraded from a contamination hit to a counter on the stated assumption that the sandbox is always a fresh `git init` at base. That invariant is enforced by pipeline-run.sh, not by the grader, and the grader also supports an `--executor host` mode where the sandbox root is the sessions' init cwd. If a host-mode run (or a future pipeline change) leaves real history, a leak of unreleased commits or the hidden-test commit would now be silent telemetry.
findings.failure_mode: History leakage goes unflagged if the fresh-init assumption is ever violated; the only trace is a non-zero history_probes count that nothing gates on.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the downgrade but gate it on evidence: treat the probe as `git_history` contamination when executor is host, or when the sandbox's `git rev-list --count --all` at grade time exceeds the base commit count; otherwise count it. Also surface history_probes > 0 in the report as a warning.

findings.description: The degraded flag now fires only when the requested model is entirely absent from models_used. A phase in which the requested model answered once and a cheaper model produced the bulk of the output tokens (partial substitution, fallback mid-session) is no longer marked degraded; extra models are recorded as telemetry only. The arm-vs-arm comparison therefore can no longer distinguish a run executed by the pinned model from one mostly executed by another model.
findings.failure_mode: Model-substitution drift within a phase is hidden from the degraded flag and from the drift guard, weakening the batch's provenance claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Flag degraded when any non-requested model (excluding a short allowlist such as the WebFetch summariser) accounts for more than a small share of the phase's output tokens, and surface extra_models with token shares in the row rather than only in STATUS.json.
